source_text: Quaeris ergo unde sit hoc malum, quod merito malum vocatur, id est, peccatum. Respondeo, imperite nimis rogari originem rei, de cuius adhuc definitione non constitit. Videamus ergo prius utrum sit, tunc quid sit, ultimum unde sit. Feci hoc quidem in primo praesentis operis libello; sed ibi ex aliqua parte securus: ambigatur ergo utrum sit malum.
pass_a_gloss: You ask therefore from where this evil is, which is deservedly called evil, that is, sin. I reply that the origin of a thing is asked too unskillfully, about whose definition it has not yet stood. Let us see therefore first whether it is, then what it is, last from where it is. I did this indeed in the first little book of the present work; but there secure from some part: let it therefore be doubted whether there is evil.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS meritum; Blaise; glossary: desert not treasury-of-merit
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis
LS opus; Blaise God's works vs devil's

pass_b_english: You therefore ask where this evil comes from which rightly deserves the name evil: sin. I reply that it is exceedingly unskilled to ask the origin of something whose definition has not yet been established. Let us first see whether it exists, then what it is, and last where it comes from. I did this in the first book of the present work, but there I proceeded with some points already secure. Let us now question whether evil exists.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
